The jobs key takes a LIST, never a map. Alternatively use a top-level map of job name to configuration. Do not mix the two shapes.

Schedules support five-field cron (weekday 0-6; no names, no `/` steps inside ranges), @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly, and every <Go duration> (every 15m, every 24h - not every 1d). A flow's `on: schedule: { cron: ... }` takes the same vocabulary; the write gate and `benmore check` refuse one the scheduler can't evaluate (it would never fire), a missing on.event op or one other than insert/update/delete (it would run on insert), a second trigger in the same `on:` (only the first is used), an unknown on.request `mode:` (it would run inline) and an unrecognized `auth:` value (it reads as required; `true`/`yes` mean required, `false`/`no`/`public` mean none). Deployed files keep loading and log a warning.

Each job does exactly one thing: `flow:` (a flow by name), `sql:` (one statement, shorthand for a one-step run), or an inline step list (run or its steps alias, not both). Both shapes take the same keys. Inline steps use the legacy step fields such as `sql:`; a `run:`/`with:` step is not recognized there (`step N has no recognized action`), so those belong in the flow the job references.

`flow:` must name a flow the app defines: flows/<name>.yaml with one job is named <name>, a flows.yaml job by its key. The write gate and `benmore check` refuse an unknown name (a deployed job that names one fails every run with `flow not found: <name>`), and the check after a flows/<name>.yaml write reports a cron job it broke. Push the flow before cron.yaml; `benmore push` and `benmore deploy` order a batch that way.
Jobs have no caller session. Do not depend on user_id or an HTTP role gate for scheduled authorization; select and scope target rows explicitly.

Live views: a cron write to a tenant-keyed table reaches only admins unless the statement RETURNs the tenant column (`UPDATE bookings SET stale = 1 WHERE ... RETURNING studio_id`); then each tenant the written rows name gets the {table, action} event. See api({at:'flows'}) → realtime_events.

A job's SQL writes fire no hooks.yaml entry (no `notify:`, `email:` or `webhook:`) and no `on: event` flow; only auto-CRUD and the other writes in api({at:'hooks'}) → triggers do. To tell a user something from a job, add `run: notify` to its flow (api({at:'flows'}) → notify_step).

A job's SQL reads and writes rows and may change the app's own tables; it cannot create, drop or alter a framework object (`_benmore_*`). The write gate and `benmore check` refuse a cron.yaml whose `sql:` is such a statement, on the job or in an inline step; a deployed job with one fails each run with `app SQL may not ...`. See api({at:'schema'}) → framework_tables.
max_attempts defaults to 1. A larger value opts into retries, so make external effects and writes idempotent first.

A job takes only schedule, flow | sql | run | steps, max_attempts and monitor (plus id in the jobs list). There is no enabled/disabled switch (remove the job to stop it) and no timezone (schedules use the server process's local time zone); the write gate and `benmore check` refuse any other key, since the scheduler would ignore it.
A malformed configuration rejects startup/reload. Check the loaded job and durable job outcome, and assert processed row counts; a successful empty loop does not prove that work ran.
